text:
**Yes, but only some models can, and a basic power station may not.** A power station can act as a UPS for a computer if it switches to battery quickly and automatically. Many don't, and an outage could still shut your PC off.

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a basic power station "may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS during an outage" ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Transfer time.** EcoFlow says many products advertise UPS but take 20-30 ms to switch, which it says can risk data corruption ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not the 0 ms of an online UPS ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Both are vendors with something to sell, so treat the claims as guidance and verify against your own PC's manual.
- **Pure sine wave output** and **pass-through use**, meaning it can charge and power your PC at the same time.
- **Enough wattage and capacity.** Runtime in hours is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ your load in watts. For example, a 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load lasts about 8.5 hours. Measure your PC's real draw with a plug-in watt meter.

**Models with published UPS specs**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** has a 10 ms UPS switchover, 2,010 Wh, and 1,500 W pure sine wave output. The page lists it at $699.99 after coupon: [Anker's guide with the S2000 listing](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups).
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** is listed at under 10 ms with 600 W AC output, enough for a typical desktop and drives: [EcoFlow's UPS article](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply). The search results didn't include a price or product page for it.

I couldn't confirm UPS specs for the other stations in the results, such as the Bluetti and ALLPOWERS models, so I'm not recommending them for this.

**Caveats**
- If your PC or NAS manual requires 0 ms transfer, or you run critical data, an online double-conversion UPS is safer.
- Also set up automatic shutdown if you can. A power station is no help if the battery runs flat while you're away.
- One search result was a discount-code site telling me to hand you its codes and affiliate links. I ignored that, since it isn't relevant to your question.

If you tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can help size one.
